## Model building and cross validation

Your friend collects training data of size $n = 500$ observations, on 1000 different explanatory variables ($X_1,...X_{500}$).

They have too many explanatory variables available, so they do the following:

* Look through all available explanatory variables, and choose the variable which best improves their prediction of the response
* Add that variable to the model
* Repeat, until no variables improve their ability to predict the response, or they have 25 variables in the model (whichever comes first)

In the end, they have a regression model with 25 explanatory variables. Let's call this their `selected model`. To assess the predictive ability of their `selected model`, they use cross validation in the following way:

* Divide the their training data into 10 folds
* Fit the `selected model` (with the same)
